Plyushchivka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mykolaiv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Founded in 1809, Plyushchivka was a Jewish agricultural colony whose population grew to over 2,000 — as much as 94 percent of the settlement — by 1897, supporting synagogues, schools, and even a meteorological station. Facing repeated pogrom threats, some colonist families emigrated to Argentina in the early 20th century; those who remained endured further violence during the Civil War and famine in the early 1920s before Soviet agricultural aid helped rebuild the community into one of the region's most prosperous collective farms by the mid-1930s. The old cemetery was destroyed in September 1941, the same period Nazi forces murdered 519 Jews here; relatives erected a memorial to the victims in 1961.
